title: Inductive Link Prediction on N-ary Relational Facts via Semantic Hypergraph Reasoning

problem.claim: Link prediction for n-ary relational facts must support predictions involving previously unseen entities.

gap.claim: Existing methods are mainly transductive and entity-embedding-based, limiting fully inductive prediction and the capture of entity-independent logical rules.

contributions.claim: An n-ary subgraph reasoning framework is proposed for fully inductive link prediction on n-ary relational facts.
NS-HART is developed to aggregate subgraphs and mine complex semantic correlations within them.
A score-function-optimization analysis is provided to explain NS-HART's effectiveness for n-ary inductive link prediction.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly introduce the n-ary semantic hypergraph as a novel graph structure for subgraph extraction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The framework is reported to have strong inductive inference ability for capturing n-ary patterns.
Extensive experiments are reported on inductive benchmarks covering transfer reasoning with and without entity features and pairwise subgraph reasoning.
The reported results highlight the framework's superiority and NS-HART's exceptional inductive ability.

narrative_sequence.summary: N-ary relational facts encode semantic correlations among more than two entities.
Existing n-ary link-prediction methods are largely transductive and struggle with entity-independent logical rules, leaving fully inductive prediction challenging.
The paper proposes local n-ary subgraph reasoning, including a semantic hypergraph and the NS-HART aggregation network.
A score-function-optimization analysis is presented to explain NS-HART's effectiveness.
Experiments on several inductive benchmarks are reported, with results claimed to show superior performance and inductive ability.

source_observation.claim: Local subgraph reasoning is used to support fully inductive inference over n-ary relational facts.

interpretation.claim: Representing relevant local structure may reduce dependence on fixed entity identities.

application.claim: For tasks involving unseen entities, consider structure-centered representations and local reasoning mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when local subgraph reasoning fails or how its costs compare with alternatives.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, sizes, metrics, baselines, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe NS-HART's architecture or training procedure in detail.
The abstract does not provide the formal score function or details of the theoretical analysis.
